title: Ariston
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says that at the end of tractate Challah the Mishnah mentions Ariston bringing first fruits from Aspamia, which were accepted from him. In the Jerusalem Talmud, Terumot 3:2, it says, “Ariston brought fruits,” etc.

Another Ariston is mentioned in Yevamot, at the end of chapter 16: “One Ariston asked R' Mana: Does this not conflict with R' Shimon ben Lakish?” Mevo Ha Yerushalmi, in his entry, interprets this as an important person.

notes.text: The notice has Aspamia; the complete Mishnah has Apamea and explicitly places the case in Syria. That geographic difference is retained as a source question. The later Ariston may instead be an honorific, according to the cited Mevo HaYerushalmi.

The saved whole Venice Terumot 3:2 scalar explicitly has Ariston bringing produce, leaving some in the sack and separating terumah; only the source's abbreviated words are translated, not the entire named narrative. The earlier complete Mishnah comparison of Apamea in Syria is inherited beside supplied Aspamia; no Spain identification is imposed. Another Ariston in the later notice remains separate. End chapter 16 is the contextual reading of ספט״ז; the corpus is inferred, not explicit there. Mevo Ha Yerushalmi's important-person explanation is attributed. The source's negative question does this NOT conflict is preserved, and uninspected personal title components remain R'.

Hyman's printed notice (vol. I, p. 243) gives Aspamia. Mishnah Challah 4:11 reads Apamea and explains the acceptance by reference to Syria. The Venice Terumot passage concerns produce and terumah. In Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 16:9, the consulted Hebrew has חד אריסטון, rendered “a gentleman” in the consulted English. Frankel's Mevo HaYerushalmi also interprets the later expression as an important person. That interpretation concerns the later occurrence.
